_comment: Single source of truth for ALL visual styling in the Question Bank Book pipeline - sitting-level HTML, chapter-wise HTML, and the final merged whole-book HTML all read from this ONE file. Change a value here, re-run generate_style_css.py, and every already-generated HTML file picks up the change automatically via its shared <link> to book-style.css - no HTML file ever needs hand-editing or regenerating for a pure style change. Page-geometry fields are included now for forward compatibility with the final print/paginated book stage (see CLAUDE.md section 7) even though the sitting-level HTML in first_run/output/ does not yet use paged.js pagination - it's a browser-reviewed content record at this stage, not a print artifact yet.

typography._chapter_print_comment: Applied only in the merged QUESTION-BANK-BOOK.html, as an additive override on top of the 34 chapter files' own embedded style (never edits those files -- see qb_common.py's print_layer_css()). Added 2026-07-26 on Pranav's explicit instruction to shrink the printed book to cut printing cost; the chapter files' own style has no explicit body font-size at all (defaults to the browser's 16px), so this is the main lever alongside the page-margin cut above.

spacing._chapter_print_comment: Same additive-override mechanism as typography's chapter_print_* fields above -- tightens the 34 chapter files' own .qblock spacing only inside the merged print output, print cost reduction, 2026-07-26.

page_geometry_for_future_print_stage._comment: Now used by first_run/scripts/qb_common.py's print_layer_css() for the merged QUESTION-BANK-BOOK.html (2026-07-26). Margins cut from 20mm to 6mm on Pranav's explicit instruction to reduce printing cost (page count is the main cost driver) -- 6mm is near the physical floor most consumer laser/inkjet printers can actually print to without clipping (many can't guarantee below ~4-5mm on all edges); true 0mm risks losing content off the edge on real hardware even though it would render fine in a PDF viewer. Go lower only after confirming the actual print method (a print shop / commercial printer with true edge-to-edge or bleed printing can safely go tighter than a home/office printer can).
